description: We are Adiya, Kristina, and Tomiris. Three people, a ton of ideas, and one shared goal: to create something truly amazing. We love exploring complex topics, experimenting, and finding solutions where others see only problems. Sometimes our ideas sound crazy, and sometimes even we have no idea how things will turn out — but that’s exactly what makes it exciting.
summary: LUMEN is an intelligent, personalized health-monitoring system designed for astronauts during long-duration space missions. It combines a wearable biosensor for analyzing physiological indicators and biochemical markers, an AI-powered platform, and a digital twin of the human body to detect potential health abnormalities at an early stage. details:
LUMEN is an intelligent, personalized health-monitoring system designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It combines a wearable biosensor, an AI-powered platform, and a digital twin of the human body to monitor health indicators and identify potential abnormalities at an early stage.

How it works:
The wearable biosensor is designed to collect physiological data, including skin moisture, electrical conductivity, and optical signals, as well as analyze selected biochemical indicators in sweat, such as cortisol and electrolytes. Its proposed sensing technology uses a LIG/MIP-based electrochemical electrode. The collected data is transmitted to the digital platform, where AI analyzes changes over time and compares them with each astronaut's individual baseline. The digital twin visualizes health indicators, their history, and potential warning signs.

The platform also integrates information from external sources, including laboratory tests, eye examinations, radiation dosimeters, and sensorimotor assessments. This allows LUMEN to provide a more comprehensive overview of astronaut health rather than relying on a single wearable device.

Benefits and intended impact:
LUMEN aims to reduce dependence on separate manual measurements, support continuous health observation, and help medical teams recognize possible health problems earlier. It focuses on several important areas, including cardiovascular, endocrine, immune, and visual health. In the future, the system could also be adapted for remote environments on Earth, such as polar research stations and isolated medical facilities.

Technology and development:
The proposed hardware architecture includes an ESP32 microcontroller, physiological sensors, a flexible sensor platform, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), and an experimental LIG/MIP electrochemical sensing element. The software platform is designed using React and JavaScript, with Python considered for backend processing and AI-based analysis. Data storage can be implemented using SQLite or PostgreSQL. The prototype development environment includes Visual Studio Code.

An additional innovation is the exploration of thermoelectric energy harvesting, which could convert part of the astronaut's body heat into electrical energy. This could supplement a rechargeable energy-storage system and reduce the device's dependence on frequent charging.

Creativity and innovation:
LUMEN brings together wearable biosensing, experimental materials science, AI-based analysis, digital human modeling, and energy harvesting in one integrated system. Its creative approach is not simply to measure health indicators, but to connect them, analyze individual trends, and provide a more complete picture of an astronaut's health.

Factors considered:
Our team considered the specific challenges of spaceflight: microgravity, radiation exposure, limited resources, restricted crew time, energy efficiency, device comfort, and the need for reliable measurements. We also recognize that the proposed cortisol sensor, energy-harvesting system, and performance in microgravity require further experimental validation.

LUMEN's long-term goal is to make astronaut health monitoring more integrated, autonomous, and personalized, supporting safer and more sustainable long-duration space exploration.
